title: Brethren, Beloved for Jesus' Sake
description: Brethren, Beloved for Jesus' Sake in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 726 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the Hymns of Zion.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bre-thren, be-loved for Je-sus' sake, A hear-ty wel-come here re-ceive; May we to-ge-ther now par-take The joys which he a-lone can give.

lines: The joys which he alone can give.
May he by whose kind care we meet,
Send his good Spirit from above,
Make our communion pure and sweet,
And cause our hearts to burn with love.
When thus we meet, to pray and praise;
We but desire to speak of him,
And of his holy word and ways.
Thus as the moments pass away,
We'll love, and wonder and adore;
Then hasten on, the glorious day,
When we shall meet to part no more.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
